products.name: Freepik AI
products.note: Stock image AI generation; commercial licensing; EU-hosted; content moderation

reading.body:
Freepik's only listed AI product is an image and graphic design tool, and the data records no compute, data center, or power details for the company at all.

The product note is where the substance sits. Freepik AI is described as stock image generation with commercial licensing, EU hosting, and content moderation. Those three attributes point in different directions. Commercial licensing makes the output usable in paid work, which is what separates a stock library from a demo. EU hosting is a placement decision, and placement is the part of an AI product that touches buildings and power, though the data does not say where the capacity comes from or how large it is. Content moderation is a policy layer, not an infrastructure one.

For AI scaling, the useful signal is the category. Image generation is inference-heavy and continuous rather than a one-time training run, so a product like this consumes power for as long as it has users. That makes it a small but real load on whatever grid serves its EU hosting. The data does not quantify that load, does not name a provider, and does not say whether Freepik owns or rents the compute.

What the record does not cover is most of what a compute-focused reader would want. There is no training detail, no model provenance, no capacity figure, no energy figure, and no mention of any constraint the company has hit. The entry is a product listing, not an infrastructure profile, and it should be read as one.
